hints: Look closely at what you actually see on each slide. No cells at all on slide 1 means they have burst, while crinkled cells on slide 2 means they have shrunk a little.
Remember water always moves by osmosis from higher (less negative) water potential to lower (more negative) water potential. Decide which way water moved on each slide to cause bursting or shrinking.
walkthrough:
**Interpret what happened to the cells**

Think like a detective. Slide 1 has no cells visible, so they must have taken in so much water that they swelled and burst. This is haemolysis.

Slide 2 cells are still there but crinkled, so they must have lost a little water and shrunk. This is crenation.

**Apply the water potential rule**

The golden rule is simple. Water moves by osmosis from high $\Psi$ (less negative, more water, dilute salt) to low $\Psi$ (more negative, less water, concentrated salt).

$$\text{net movement of water: high } \Psi \rightarrow \text{ low } \Psi$$

**Match each slide to the correct gradient**

For slide 1, water moved IN, so the outside must have higher $\Psi$ than the inside. That means the $\Psi$ of the cell was more negative than the $\Psi$ of the external solution.

For slide 2, water moved OUT, so the outside must have lower $\Psi$ than the inside. That means the $\Psi$ of the external solution was more negative than the $\Psi$ of the cell. Only row B says both of these correctly.

options.A: Slide 1 part is true, bursting is due to swelling, but slide 2 part is backwards. If cell $\Psi$ was more negative than external, water would move in, not out to cause crinkling.
options.B: Perfect match. Slide 1 water enters because cell $\Psi$ is more negative than dilute external solution, causing bursting. Slide 2 water leaves because external $\Psi$ is more negative than cell, causing slight crenation.
options.C: Slide 1 is wrong. If cell $\Psi$ was less negative (higher) than external, water would leave the cell, so cells would shrink, not disappear by bursting.
options.D: Slide 1 describes water entry which fits bursting, but slide 2 is wrong. If cell $\Psi$ was slightly more negative than external, there would be slight net entry, not the net loss needed for crinkled cells.
